patch.diff:31-61 adds Lambda to monai/transforms/utility/array.py as a pure append; patch.diff:62-124 adds Lambdad and the LambdaD alias to dictionary.py.

No tests were run for this experiment; the judgment rests on reading the code. The patch is additions only: no existing lines are removed or changed except the typing import line in dictionary.py (patch.diff:70-71, extended with Callable).
Lambda is placed in monai/transforms/utility/array.py:296, the array-level vanilla transform module, matching the reference location.
Lambdad is placed in monai/transforms/utility/dictionary.py:417, matching the reference location.

Docs are in docs/source/transforms.rst under the Vanilla (line 346) and Dictionary-based (line 704) sections, the same sections the reference uses. Tests are at tests/test_lambda.py and tests/test_lambdad.py, matching the reference file names.

Lambda.__init__(self, func: Callable) -> None with assert callable(func) at array.py:311-312 and __call__(self, img) returning self.func(img) at array.py:315-316. This matches the reference signature and behavior.

Lambdad.__init__(self, keys: KeysCollection, func: Callable) -> None at dictionary.py:436 calls super().__init__(keys), then self.lambd = Lambda(func) at dictionary.py:438. __call__(self, data) at dictionary.py:440-444 returns a new dict, the same contract as the reference.
The alias LambdaD = LambdaDict = Lambdad at dictionary.py:460 is the registration the reference adds. The reference adds no Lambda alias for the array class, and neither does the candidate.

dictionary.py:39 imports Lambda from monai.transforms.utility.array, the same direction the existing dictionary wrappers use (dictionary.py:29-40 imports array-level transforms). The array module does not import the dictionary module.
dictionary.py:24-26 keeps the existing imports from monai.config, monai.transforms.compose, and monai.utils.misc. No new cross-layer imports are introduced.
Lambdad subclasses MapTransform (dictionary.py:417), and the alias LambdaD = LambdaDict = Lambdad is at dictionary.py:460, which the base dictionary alias block (base dictionary.py tail) follows.

dictionary.py:19 adds Callable to the typing import. monai/transforms/__init__.py:21-22 re-exports via 'from .utility.array import *' and 'from .utility.dictionary import *'. array.py and dictionary.py define no __all__, so the new classes are exported without further registration. The reference relies on the same mechanism.
Docs registration is in docs/source/transforms.rst:346-351 and 704-709.

The patch adds no third-party or new internal dependencies. The only import changes are the typing Callable (dictionary.py:19) and the Lambda import (dictionary.py:39), both from already-used modules.
Tests import only numpy, unittest, monai.transforms.utility.*, and tests.utils.NumpyImageTestCase2D, which are existing test dependencies (tests/test_lambda.py:12-18, tests/test_lambdad.py:12-18).

Per-value behavior lives in the array-level Lambda (array.py:296). The dictionary wrapper Lambdad (dictionary.py:417) only maps keys and delegates to self.lambd (dictionary.py:443). This is the same split the reference uses, and the same split existing wrappers use.
No logic is duplicated across the two layers.

Lambda subclasses Transform, the same base as the other array transforms (array.py:296). Lambdad subclasses MapTransform and passes keys through super().__init__(keys) (dictionary.py:436-437), using the existing key-validation path in compose.py:235-242.
The implementation uses the existing MapTransform/Transform extension points with no parallel mechanism.

Lambdad copies the input with d = dict(data) at dictionary.py:441, then writes only the listed keys. The caller's dict is not mutated, which the test checks at tests/test_lambdad.py:31-33 (assertIsNot for identity, and the original data kept for slicing).
The new code does not reach into MapTransform internals or Compose; it uses self.keys from the base class (dictionary.py:442).
The 'd' suffix on the dictionary class and the Name = NameDict = Namedd alias follow the convention at dictionary.py:460 and base dictionary.py tail (IdentityD/AsChannelFirstD style).
Assert-with-message at array.py:312 matches array.py:55, 114, 134 conventions. Copyright headers match the 'Copyright 2020 MONAI Consortium' header used in the repo.

Google-style Args blocks appear in the Lambda (array.py:296-310) and Lambdad (dictionary.py:417-435) docstrings. Line lengths are within the 120-column limit (setup.cfg:38, pyproject.toml:2); a scan of added lines found none over 120.

Test method names (test_identity, test_slicing) differ from the reference (test_lambda_identity, test_lambda_slicing). This is a style difference, not a convention violation. The candidate's assertions (np.testing.assert_equal, assertIsNot) are standard in the repo.
Lambda applies the callable to the whole input unchanged and returns its result (array.py:315-316), matching the reference behavior and docs ('receives the whole input value').

Lambdad applies a single callable to each listed key and returns a new dict with the same contract as the reference (dictionary.py:440-444). Shallow dict copy matches the reference (reference dictionary.py: d = dict(data)).

The candidate's doc examples (array.py:300-306, dictionary.py:421-429) produce [[1, 2], [6, 7]] for arange(10).reshape(2,5)[:,1:3], which I traced by hand. No CI doctest wiring exists (grep of .github and runtests.sh found none), so these are documentation only.
The candidate adds only the alias LambdaD/LambdaDict. The reference does the same, so no alias is missing relative to the reference.
